title: Wave-based release orchestration and acceptance criteria for enterprise private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As we move more customers to Private (VPC/on‑prem) offerings, we need a prescriptive, repeatable wave-based release orchestration plan with clear acceptance and rollback criteria. The goal is to reduce upgrade/regression incidents, shorten mean time to detect (MTTD) for regressions, and provide a playbook product teams can reuse when shipping infra or runtime changes that affect private customers.

Scope: This ticket covers definition and alignment of: (1) Wave composition (canary -> pilot -> broad), (2) Concrete acceptance criteria per wave (SLOs, error budgets, perf regressions, compatibility checks), (3) Automated pre-flight checks and post-rollout telemetry dashboards, (4) Rollback and mitigation triggers, (5) Customer communication and support playbook, (6) Staging environment sizing and compatibility matrix validation. Implementation (automation) will be handled by ENG follow-ups.

Deliverables: 
- Wave taxonomy document (canary, pilot, wave sizes, eligibility rules) and decision table.
- Acceptance criteria checklist: latency 95th < pre-roll + 15ms OR < 200ms absolute (whichever stricter), error rate increase < 0.1% absolute, end-to-end job success > 99.5%, model inference cost variance < 10%.
- Rollback rules: automatic rollback if error budget consumed > 50% in 30m window OR sustained latency violation for 3 consecutive 5m windows.
- Observability: per-customer and per-wave dashboards with token-level cost, latency, and error breakdown; automated alerting runbooks wired to on-call.
- Customer signals: ingestion of customer-reported incidents, post-wave CSAT survey template, and support escalation matrix.
- Playbook: runbook and Slack/Email templates for notifying customers in each wave and declaring a pause/rollback.

Acceptance criteria (this ticket): 
- PM/Eng/Design sign-off on wave taxonomy and acceptance thresholds.
- Confluence page with runbook and measurable SLA checks linked to dashboards.
- Owners for automation tasks identified and ENG tickets created for implementation.

Success metrics: 
- First full wave rollout completed for a pilot customer with zero Sev1 regressions.
- Reduction in private upgrade incidents by 40% vs last quarter.
- Time-to-rollback median < 20 minutes for any automated rollback events.

Risks and trade-offs: 
- Tight thresholds slow rollouts and increase manual effort; looser thresholds increase customer risk. Recommend starting conservative for first two quarters then relaxing with stronger automation.
- Staging parity is imperfect for some on‑prem environments; include a compatibility matrix and require a pre-flight smoke test run by customer.

Stakeholders: 
- Product: Aisha (owner), Luca (release owner)
- Eng: Runtime release, infra, telemetry leads
- Design: rollout UX for Console communications
- Support/CS: escalation and customer-facing comms
- Legal/Compliance: for air-gapped customers

Next steps: 
1) Alignment meeting with ENG/Design/Support (scheduled 2026-03-05).
2) Publish wave taxonomy draft to Confluence and solicit feedback by 2026-03-10.
3) Create ENG implementation tickets for automation and dashboards.
